BBC News — "'Burnham's triple shock' and 'City face expulsion'", published 30 September 2026, 01:10 BST (Exa metadata 2026-09-30T01:10:19Z). The BBC's own newspaper review, which is the approved route to reporting what banned papers lead on. Text via Exa search highlights.

"Every front page on Wednesday is dominated by Prime Minister Andy Burnham's speech at the Labour Party
conference."

- DAILY MAIL (banned paper, reported via the BBC): describes it as "the most Left-wing speech by a PM since
  1970s". Front page: "Burnham's triple shock".
- DAILY TELEGRAPH: "Triple lock scrapped by 2030". Reports the plan would replace the triple lock with a
  double lock, meaning the state pension would increase by either inflation or a minimum of 2.5%, with the
  link to wage growth scrapped. Also carries a Manchester City football story. [SPORT — EXCLUDED.]
- THE TIMES: Burnham is staking his future on "free care for all"; he admitted there would be a "political
  price" but "someone has to go through the pain barrier and rip the plaster off". Describes the 70-MINUTE
  speech as a "high-stakes gamble to win Labour a second term in power", and notes it ALSO saw Burnham
  PLEDGE TO REOPEN THE BREXIT DEAL WITH EUROPE and reform the voting system.
- EXPRESS (banned): launching a "crusade" to save the triple lock, saying he is betraying pensioners and
  betraying Brexit. "It's a crying shame for our nation."
- THE SUN (banned): "Locky horror show".
- THE I PAPER (banned): key details of the "extraordinary" speech, which it says saw cabinet ministers in
  tears; "billions are expected to be saved".
- DAILY STAR (banned): "Burnham picks the lock".
- METRO (banned): "Andy's rallying cry".

NOTE: the Brexit pledge is NEW to our coverage. It was not in last night's edition and is flagged by both
The Times front page and Politico as one of the three most radical announcements, alongside the triple lock
and electoral reform.
